Three months ago, we had our cat hospitalized after two months of trying to treat her at a regular daytime vet clinic. She had been anorexic for eight weeks, was dehydrated, and had lost half her weight. Given her condition, they admitted her for a minimum of two days. The next morning (about 6 PM) they called me to come pick her up because they had apparently miraculously saved her. The results showed nothing, and the IV fluids had rehydrated her somewhat, so there was no risk of relapse, with frightening certainty (I asked four times). In the end, 30 minutes after leaving, she relapsed... During those first 24 hours, we were asked to confirm by email an authorization for further examination, specifically an abdominal ultrasound. This had to be confirmed that evening to ensure the cat would be fasted the following morning, which we did. When we picked her up after the ultrasound and read the reports, the results were "of limited reliability due to the animal not being fasted." We were charged for a botched, unreliable exam, and since nothing was detected (understandable, given the poor work), they sent her back to us claiming they had performed miracles. They had her readmitted for 24 hours, charging us for a chest CT scan because, after playing with her life, the poor thing developed a minor cardiac arrhythmia. Imagine being shuttled around, given IV fluids, brought home, and readmitted; I think even a human who understands would start to feel a little anxious. So, on top of everything else, a stolen exam—classy!

In the end, they're now talking about the risk of cancer, with exorbitant costs, and a vet who speaks with incredible contempt, considering the 48 hours we've just been through. And all this culminates in three different vets who haven't once said the same thing about our pet and who literally played with its life and demonstrated professional negligence. I think that beyond basic practices, like selling you deworming medication or administering a vaccine, they lack the skills to do more, let alone the necessary humanity.

Update: The clinic is giving a false response to this comment, claiming they suspended my pet's hospitalization because she was better. However, the ultrasound, which could have diagnosed the problem despite her very brief, even fleeting, return of appetite, was botched... I have a photo to prove it. Don't take your pets there; they couldn't care less about their health and charge exorbitant fees (under the guise of investing in cutting-edge equipment) for not knowing how to perform the procedure. Thank goodness you didn't charge double hospitalization fees when you should never have let her out! It's pure and simple fraud... it couldn't be simpler.

Excellent care was provided today, October 9th, by a veterinarian whose name I don't know. She quickly identified the abscess caused by a foxtail that my old chow chow was suffering from and treated it very well. The most competent vet I've seen in 12 years! And very kind too, thank you!

We were very well received and cared for; the staff were kind and did everything they could to save Nala, who unfortunately arrived in a very critical condition. They guided and supported us through Nala's final days. So thank you nonetheless.

My ten-year-old dog, following an incident, was paralyzed in her hindquarters and could barely walk. I went to this address on October 2nd at 3:15 PM, and they refused to take her for an X-ray, or even for a consultation! The excuse: you didn't make an appointment! Since when do you need to make an appointment at the Emergency Room? My regular veterinarian (who wasn't there on October 2nd and doesn't have an X-ray machine) was shocked to learn of this behavior and told me she's going to report them. You can remove the word "EMERGENCY" from the front of your establishment.

Ms. Buenestado, thank you so much for your excellent review of our veterinary clinic. Your satisfaction with our animal health services is our greatest reward.

We hope to see you again soon for all your veterinary needs.

See you soon!
The UCVET Team

Hello Mr. Mizrahi, thank you so much for your 5-star review. We are delighted that our service met your expectations.
Please feel free to share your experiences with our team to help us continue providing the best veterinary care.
See you soon!

The UCVET Team
Amazing experience here. Seen almost immediately by attentive and caring staff.
Professional team

The care at this clinic is exceptional.

The kindness, attentiveness, and concern shown to the animal (even cleaning him up after he had an accident in his carrier when I only asked for paper towels) AND to the owner are truly outstanding.

Special mention must also be made of the billing for an emergency service, without trying to take advantage of people's distress to sell them unnecessary procedures or services, which is far from the case with all the emergency clinics I've had to visit.

I came in as an emergency on the recommendation of my veterinarian for an ultrasound on my cat, whose general condition was extremely alarming.

After the procedure, I received a thorough debriefing, clearly explaining that my cat's chances of survival were very uncertain, without trying to hide this reality to sell me overpriced additional procedures.

I was able to get complete information about my cat's chances of survival based on the various possible diagnoses, the cost of potential further investigations, what they would reveal, and the treatments (and their costs) that would be implemented. This allowed me to make informed decisions.

I ultimately chose to proceed with a further analysis at a controlled cost, which would allow for a better assessment of whether my cat was suffering from a serious illness or not.

In the end, the proposed second investigations revealed that my cat did not have a serious condition, all for a cost that, while not insignificant, was reasonable.

If needed, I will certainly return.
Thank you again.
A deplorable experience. My pet's hospitalization was traumatic. A money-making operation that prioritizes profit over animal welfare.

A deeply shocking experience, both medically and emotionally. Upon arrival, a veterinarian presented me with a quote of over €800 "just to start," including a battery of tests, without even taking the time to review my pet's medical records or properly examine him. The consultation was rushed.

My pet spent several days hospitalized in a state of extreme stress. Tests performed only 36 hours earlier by our regular veterinarian were repeated, without any clear explanation of their purpose. Even worse, the medical file subsequently sent by UCVet contained glaring errors, confirming that the documents provided, including the health record, had not been reviewed.

Medications were administered even though corresponding injections had already been given by our regular veterinarian 36 hours prior. This type of situation is particularly worrying when dealing with an already weakened animal.

To make matters worse, the vet displayed a profound lack of empathy. When the cost of hospitalization was discussed, the veterinarian was particularly rude and made sarcastic remarks about people who can't afford thousands of euros in veterinary care.

I felt that the care was driven more by the accumulation of billed tests and treatments than by a proportionate, coordinated approach truly focused on the animal's well-being. We are still left without answers or a diagnosis.

My pet left this hospitalization deeply traumatized, even though he was already ill and vulnerable.

Veterinary hospitalization should be a place of care, rigor, and empathy. This experience was unfortunately the complete opposite.

Excellent clinic, very good advice and care for my cat. Attentive and caring reception staff ensure everything goes smoothly for the animal, and the veterinarian takes the time to explain and advise. I highly recommend them.

Hello Ms. Bouliol,

Thank you for your message, and we hope Ryu is feeling better.

Have a good day.

I'm a regular customer because I take my cats there several times.
One of them had surgery at this clinic.

My pet is still being followed by the clinic and has not yet left, but I can only praise the professionalism, kindness, communication and daily explanations of my pet's condition, which was hospitalized, by the various veterinarians I spoke to online, and I thank them for that.
In an emergency, you can go there without hesitation. Very convenient in the evenings and on weekends. Price-wise, it's an emergency clinic. That's to be expected.

The UCVET Team
Very satisfied with Dr. Pothier who treated my dog ​​with professionalism and great empathy.

Quick appointment, excellent service.
I recommend them.

Dear Mr. Duverne,

Sincerely,

Very satisfied with the emergency consultation for my dog.
The appointment was on time and he was seen perfectly.
I was also very happy with the reception.

I sadly had to say goodbye to my beloved 14-year-old cat, Hortense, a few days ago. I want to sincerely thank Dr. Sieklucka, thanks to whom this incredibly painful moment unfolded with the utmost gentleness, kindness, and patience. Her words, explanations, and empathy were a great help. In my immense grief, I have at least the consolation that this farewell was dignified and peaceful. Thank you, Dr. Sieklucka, and all the best.
Alright

On July 14th, we called to schedule an appointment at the clinic.
We arrived at 10:15 am. Two people were seen, then no one else. The receptionist walked by, ignored us, and took other patients. I asked her about it, and she apologized for forgetting us, saying she hadn't seen our cat. After an hour and a half, she decided we could wait another 30 minutes, without changing the order of arrival, because she had other emergencies... but how could she possibly assess our animal in its cage without even seeing it?
The cat's mouth was open from dehydration... which is to be expected after an hour and a half.

But the receptionist seems more competent in event planning than in handling animals. In short, she lacked any logical thinking and acted like she'd done everything perfectly. So, she was completely incompetent. Unfortunately, I can't judge the veterinarians since I didn't see them. This clinic should be avoided for the time being. My contact information is on file...if the vets want it...ultimately, I paid €519 for emergency care at another clinic in Maisons-Alfort...perfect.

Thank you to the entire team for taking such good care of Pepito in the emergency room from 4 a.m. Sunday until his discharge on Tuesday.

Understanding our concern, you provided us with all the necessary information and possible developments with great sensitivity and tact.
Pepito is doing much better thanks to your discharge recommendations.
A huge thank you, and I won't hesitate to come back to see you if needed (but hopefully not for a very long time for an emergency :-)). It's a shame I live outside of Paris because you would have become the official doctors for my four-legged gang.
Thank you all!

My injured cat received efficient, compassionate, and prompt care. The treatment and transparency were excellent. The team was attentive to both human and animal patients, and aware of the trauma experienced by both. Thank you for Ariel, who I hope will not suffer any lasting effects from her surgery.

I share this opinion with great sadness. My cat unfortunately had to be euthanized after a rapid decline in her health.

During previous consultations, her breathing difficulties were attributed to bronchitis. Subsequently, I was informed that she was actually experiencing heart failure and that her symptoms were related to a heart condition.

I was deeply affected to learn of this diagnosis so late, and I regret that this possibility wasn't identified earlier, as it might have allowed for a different approach to her care. This situation has been extremely painful and leaves me with a profound sense of incomprehension. I will avoid your clinic in the future.

Hello Jérôme,
Thank you for this very positive review!
With our best wishes to you and your pet,
The Veterinary Team

Inconsistent caregivers. During emergency hours (nights and weekends), they are very friendly and attentive.

During regular hours, they are very apathetic.

At 12:15 PM, I was asked to decide whether or not to euthanize my cat "by the end of the morning." Perhaps we need to revisit the definition of "morning" and reconsider how to communicate with a human being who is dealing with the possible death of their companion?

Mr. Kerchouche, thank you for your positive 4-star rating.

I would like to express my sincere gratitude to the entire team at the Medical Clinic, as well as to the veterinary nurses who cared for my beloved dog, Fonzie.

Despite the incredibly painful decision I had to make—a decision that still weighs heavily on my heart, even though I know it was the right one—I will always cherish the memory of your gentle support and the quality of care provided since January.

In this moment suspended between love and grief, you were a precious presence. I especially thank Dr. Wiktoria Sieklucka for her great professionalism, but above all for her attentive listening, her kindness, and the incredibly humane way she cared for both Fonzie and me.

Fonzie was fortunate to be surrounded by such caring hands. Thanks to you, her final moments were filled with dignity and peace.

Thank you from the bottom of my heart for your human values, your quiet compassion, and your dedication. These are lights I will never forget and that will continue to accompany the memory of my faithful companion.

Thank you to the entire veterinary team for your warm welcome and kindness, even though we arrived too late to tweet. Thank you to the receptionist and the veterinarian I spoke to earlier and again this morning about our other dog who was sick, probably due to what happened last night. You reassured me and gave me advice on the phone, and thank you again.
Clinic with attentive and competent staff
Very welcoming, bright premises, separate dog and cat area. A very nice and pleasant place for animals and their owners.
The medical team and reception staff were very attentive and responsive, providing excellent support for our dog and ourselves. Osso has returned to his normal routine after the operation.
Excellent welcome. The vets were very professional and gave clear explanations. The follow-up after our dog's surgery was excellent. A veterinary clinic to recommend.

Dr. Wiktoria Sieklucka, thank you for your care of Harry. You were wonderful to him throughout his treatment.
Thank you for the sincerity of your words and for easing our pain.
We thank you from the bottom of our hearts, and what a joy it is to see the word "vocation" so beautifully embodied by you.
Thank you to you and the D'Ucvet reception staff.
Thank you for Harry.
Never go to this vet! They made me wait 5 hours only to refuse to see my cat! They speak rudely to clients, not even one star. What a disgrace to have such incompetent and inhumane professionals!

Good experience in my case. I arrived on a public holiday. I was seen at reception immediately. The wait time will depend on the number of patients, but there's nothing we can do about that. I was able to ask all my questions; it was quick and efficient. It's expensive, but that's the "Emergency" rate, so it's normal for it to be pricey.

My cat had a cardiac ultrasound performed by veterinarian Mr. Chassain, which met all my expectations. He was communicative, explained everything clearly, demonstrated a high level of expertise, was gentle with the animal, and was understanding and kind. Thank you again for this excellent appointment!

My cat was captured without my consent and then brought to this clinic by a third party two weeks later.
Thanks to the clinic staff verifying the microchip, I was able to get my cat back. Thank you for that!
There was a small issue with the billing for the treatment; after I complained, management was very responsive, and we were able to resolve the problem within a few days.

Thank you to the entire UCVET team, who saved my Kate from her illness thanks to their quick response and expertise. Thank you also for taking such good care of her during her three days in the hospital. We were able to visit her in excellent conditions and were kept informed of every step and her progress. During her check-up this week, Kate didn't stop purring when she arrived at the clinic. Fantastic clinic with fantastic veterinarians, thank you for everything!!!
Excellent, the best clinic in Paris. Expert surgeons, courteous and reactive staff. Dr WOJCICKI saved my pomeranian who had a knee problem. Incredible and highly recommend.
A really great place for animals. The vets are very competent and friendly.

We received a very warm welcome. Dr. Gaël Chassain was very gentle with our little Nala during her ultrasound. I highly recommend this clinic. Best of luck to the entire team.

We brought our dog in as an emergency in a terrible and critical condition (vomiting that had worsened over two weeks, repeated sleepless nights, partially unsuccessful tests at our regular vet's office, etc.). On the recommendation of our vet, the ultrasound was performed respectfully and gently, and the subsequent care was extremely smooth and comfortable. Every step was explained, detailed, and justified; all the staff we dealt with were empathetic and patient. It was our dog's first hospitalization, and we felt completely confident.

This confidence was confirmed the next day with an early discharge, excellent post-operative results, and a dog who was upset but not mistreated.

One last point: the Maisons-Alfort Veterinary School quoted us a bill "easily" exceeding €4,000 after a single phone call in an odious and pretentious tone, without even seeing the animal... We didn't even pay half that at UCVet, and the care was truly premium.

We highly recommend UCVet, we will return if needed and without the slightest hesitation!

Despite the facility being well-suited for veterinary care, I am extremely frustrated by the lack of professionalism and transparency. My dog ​​died two days after being hospitalized at the Ucvet clinic. Indeed, after picking him up two days after his hospitalization, he was crying out in pain. I was told it was a cry of abandonment and that it was normal after a three-day hospitalization, even though he was crying incessantly. I took him to the emergency room, where they told me his vital signs were normal, his catheter hadn't moved, and that the pain medication was working and was strong, so it couldn't be related to pain, despite the fact that he never stopped crying, even in front of them. Upon returning home from the emergency room, my dog ​​continued to cry out in pain for two days straight and died. On the last day, I went to see my vet to explain that the prescribed feeding amounts didn't seem nearly sufficient and to describe the dog's symptoms. The dog's crying wasn't normal; unfortunately, after just two hours of treatment at the vet's, he passed away.

I'm angry because you weren't at all sincere or transparent in your statements, or perhaps it was a lack of expertise. The dog suffered in his final moments when things could have turned out differently. It's a disgrace, and I wouldn't advise anyone to entrust their dog to you for treatment if their pet is in a difficult situation.

We came in for our cat who was nearing the end of his life. The vet's attentive listening and practical examinations were excellent. I highly recommend this clinic; they take great care of our four-legged companions and provide excellent support to their owners. A huge thank you to the whole team—it's very reassuring! 🫶👍💛 …
Following a two-day emergency hospitalization for our little dog, the medical care was excellent and the staff were very kind. Thank you to them.

Excellent experience at UCVET: my cat Eliot had surgery for a thyroid tumor performed by Dr. Maingaud. I thank the entire team for their kindness. Eliot stayed at the clinic for nearly 30 hours, and I was regularly updated on his condition, which reassured me. The clinic's prices are much more reasonable than at a hospital (Eliot had his scan done at Fregis), and payment plans are available. I highly recommend this team for their professionalism and their gentle approach to our four-legged friends and their owners.

First time at UCVET for my cat, who was hospitalized due to several health issues, and we were made to feel very welcome from the start. The staff are very gentle, and for a cat as stressed as mine, it was perfect.

The team took excellent care of him, and we clearly avoided a catastrophe. You saved my cat Simon's life, and I thank you immensely! I will never hesitate to come back here if I have a major problem in the future. I have complete confidence in them now. The costs were high, but he underwent numerous tests, received a great deal of medication, and spent two nights in the hospital. We were even able to return a medication we hadn't used. Despite the expense, we are very grateful, and our cat's health is priceless. He's back on his feet now, and we can sleep soundly.

(Furthermore, many preventative tests were carried out to ensure he doesn't have any serious illnesses or cancerous lesions, and we are now reassured.)

Thanks again! I hope I don't see you again soon 🤣.

The reception was very empathetic and friendly, both on the phone and in person. The veterinarians and staff were available and answered all questions directly. I highly recommend this veterinary clinic.
Excellent clinic, they've saved many animals from the Aubervilliers Animal Association and the whole team is fantastic.
A caring and professional team, a well-equipped, new, clean and neatly arranged clinic, and appropriate care for my cat's cardiac monitoring.
Everything was very good: reception, vet, follow-up.

I highly recommend this establishment. The service was pleasant and efficient. The doctor was very professional, conscientious, attentive, and a good listener.

Thank you all.

Very professional, welcoming, and caring. They are punctual, which is very important to mention. I came on the recommendation of my regular veterinarian, and I must say I was pleasantly surprised. Thank you.

Attentive and very caring staff. I recommend them 100%.

My little bulldog Luna has been treated for Addison's disease for nine years now, and it's thanks to them that she's still alive. Her illness was diagnosed when she was only four months old, even though Addison's usually only affects female dogs from the age of five! I am eternally grateful to them, and so is Luna, who is loved by everyone!

I took my cat Teddy to their V2TU clinic on a Sunday; they take over when the Ucvet clinic is closed.

So, Ucvet took over for my cat the following Monday. I had taken him in for gastroenteritis. He had to be given IV fluids and medication because he had a fever. I thank Dr. Bruguiere and her team for taking such good care of my little cat. She took the time to call me every day to keep me informed about Teddy's condition. He's been doing much better since then, and I'm delighted. Yes, there were a lot of tests, and yes, it was quite expensive, but I don't regret it. The most important thing is that he was treated.
As a veterinary assistant myself, I know that tests are necessary for diagnosis and for determining the appropriate treatment.
Thank you again to the UCVET team.

Our sick cat received prompt care, was hospitalized for two days, and was kept informed of his condition at all times. The facility is clean and welcoming, and the animals are well cared for with appropriate care and equipment, in cages suited to their needs. They were kind and efficient throughout; I highly recommend them.

I gave two stars because they saved my cat from a urinary tract infection. The procedure cost €900. Was it necessary? I don't know, so I'm not sure. After the procedure, they told me that from that day forward, if I didn't follow a very strict veterinary diet and have weekly checkups with IV fluids, my cat wouldn't make it through the year. That was the first trauma for me. The other trauma is my cat, who has to endure weekly IV fluids and no longer eats because he doesn't like any kibble or wet food. Due to lack of funds and seeing my cat unhappy, I had to stop everything. Thinking my cat was going to die, I focused on affection and gentle care at home. Five years later, my cat is still alive.
Thank you for "saving" him, but I don't thank you for being under the thumb of lobbyists and traumatizing your customers into buying your products.

Hello,
Thank you very much for your rating and for your trust.

Very, very good. They took excellent care of my pet and the prices are very reasonable.

A top-notch medical team. Kindness and clear explanations. I left my dog, Neige, there for splenectomy knowing she was in good hands.

A huge thank you to the entire medical team.
Perfect  ! electrocardiogram

We highly recommend this clinic, which has all the necessary technical and human resources to treat even the most complex illnesses in our four-legged friends.

Our beagle (Metro) stayed there for over two weeks and underwent two successive surgeries for herniated discs that had completely paralyzed him.

We went through an emotional rollercoaster, but our dog is safe and healthy. This is undoubtedly due in large part to the professionalism and kindness of the entire team. (A special thank you to Nicolas for saving our dog).

We had previously gone to another emergency clinic that sent us home with anti-inflammatories, without even considering the possibility of a herniated disc or ordering a CT scan...

Bad experience with my cat… The estimate was €200, but I paid €250… all for a consultation, blood work (biochemistry, ionogram, blood gases, but no hematology), and an injection.
The vet showed little empathy towards the pet owner, who is experiencing financial difficulties. No payment plan was offered. Of course, you're not a bank, but a little understanding wouldn't hurt!

In short, I won't be going back, especially since my cat has hyperthyroidism… and a platelet count well below average… perhaps a hematological analysis would have been necessary, wouldn't it?

Regards

In response to your message, it's true that the vet only gave a verbal estimate, but it's still a commitment.

Since it was only a verbal agreement, you were able to add the cost of medications, for example, at will, without having discussed it beforehand.

I also want to point out that, lacking the necessary funds, I had to go to a friend to borrow the money so I could pay you before receiving any treatment. The agreed-upon amount was €200, period! That's what I borrowed, and the veterinarian was fully aware of this.
These are not very ethical practices.

Regards

Hello Study Time,
We sincerely thank you for this positive review. The entire team at the veterinary clinic places great importance on client satisfaction and the medical care of their animals.

The welcome was more or less warm and attentive depending on the veterinarian.

Our cat was hospitalized in the evening around 7:00 PM. The veterinarian (who was very gentle and reassuring, by the way) who saw us at that time told us that she would have to fast until the next day so that a blood test could be done.
The next day, another veterinarian called us and gave us a rather alarming report on our cat's case. She mentioned, among all the conclusions of the tests performed, that "the blood test done at 2:00 PM is not reliable because the stomach wasn't empty," without giving us any further explanation. (We also asked if it would be wise to repeat the blood test later that afternoon.)
When we picked up our cat in the late afternoon, we reminded them that she hadn't eaten since the previous morning and that it seemed very strange to us that her stomach was still full at 2:00 PM the next day. She finally admitted that, due to a communication breakdown between the teams, our cat had been fed… This unreliable blood test, resulting from a staff error, was therefore billed to us. A serious health assessment of our cat led to a rather intensive treatment that could have been different if the tests had been more thorough.

Furthermore, when I asked the vet if she had observed whether my cat had defecated during her hospitalization, she simply replied that she "has other animals hospitalized and cannot pay attention to each one," even though we were consulting partly for gastrointestinal issues. This is, of course, understandable, but not very reassuring regarding the care our animals receive when we are not there.

Thank you nonetheless for the attention given to our pet. We would, however, have appreciated a little more honesty.

I waited 30 minutes (no problem), and the vet let me in to tell me she could do it, but the price had now doubled and the man had given me incorrect information. Emmanuelle Dollé is incredibly unprofessional and rude, and I wouldn't recommend anyone take their pets there.

Avoid at all costs! They only care about money, have no compassion, no sensitivity, and give no information. My cat died!

On Friday evening, May 31st, I took my cat to the UCVET emergency clinic because his hindquarters were wobbly. They did an X-ray, ultrasound, blood tests, etc., and told me everything was fine, but that a CT scan would be necessary because it might be neurological, and that the UCVET emergency clinic didn't have one. However, the UCVET clinic (next to the emergency room) did have a CT scanner.

I got an appointment for Tuesday morning, June 3rd. An hour after the appointment, they returned my cat in his carrier without saying a word, only that I would get the results a few days later. I arrive home, a 30-minute drive from the clinic. I take my cat out of his carrier; he's suffocating and having great difficulty breathing. I immediately call the clinic, who tell me to either wait a little while until he starts breathing with his mouth open, and if he starts breathing with his mouth open, I should come back, or to come back, but given his condition, I know he won't survive the trip. I call an emergency vet who makes house calls, and she tells me my cat is dying—oxygen mask, injection... I go with her to the nearest vet. In the car, my cat is meowing in pain. We finally arrive, but they make it clear that we have to put him down.

What do I hold against UCVET? Their incompetence. How could they give me my cat back after the scan without telling me anything and without having seen his condition? How could they not detect the slightest sign on the ultrasound and blood tests?

And I'm not even mentioning the astronomical sums they charge. 550 euros for a scan, and nearly 700 euros on Friday night in the emergency room, all for nothing, only to lose my cat!

I strongly advise against this place. One small detail: they focus heavily on their reception and cleanliness, which are undeniable, but their medical care is appalling!!
